source_snapshot.procedure: Enter BIOS Advanced/SIO Common Setting, change any settings, save/exit and verify after re-entry; source also says to clear logs.
source_snapshot.criteria: Settings can be changed and saved.
source_snapshot.deepseek: NO; correctly assigns BIOS work to an operator, but leaves the setting unnamed and adds an undefined serial effect not required by the Master criterion.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: MANUAL ONLY; constrains the mutation to an owner-approved common field/value/rollback and requests persistence plus any explicitly approved SIO effect.

historical_reviews.deepseek: The manual boundary fits, but `any settings` and `any serial effect` are not safe or measurable contracts.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Classification and exact-field controls are accepted; functional effect evidence is required only when the approved field matrix defines one, while save/re-entry persistence remains the Master checkpoint.
historical_reviews.history: Exact-code searches found no duplicate variant; adjacent SIO Configuration is separately scoped to per-device/physical-port settings.
historical_reviews.v3_1: A controller-wide common option can affect multiple SIO consumers, so one reversible field with an enumerated dependency set is safer and more auditable than an arbitrary menu change.

original_test_intent: Have a qualified operator demonstrate that one explicitly approved SIO Common Setting can be changed, saved and retained after BIOS re-entry, with affected common dependencies checked and baseline restored when required.
original_method: Bind the exact SUT, BIOS and SIO controller; capture the common-settings page and dependency baseline; after approval change only the named common option to the approved value, save/reboot/re-enter, verify persistence and any specified cross-device effect, then restore/verify baseline.
manual_activity: The owner selects one common SIO option and its dependency/rollback contract; a qualified operator performs BIOS capture, change, save/re-entry, optional approved-effect observation and restoration.
required_inputs: Exact SUT/board, BIOS and SIO-controller identity
Exact SIO Common Setting field and menu path
Baseline, approved test value and rollback value
Affected SIO functions/devices and expected effects, if any
Qualified BIOS operator and reboot approval
safety_requirements: Never treat `change any settings` as blanket authorization
Change only one named common option
Distinguish this row from adjacent per-device SIO Configuration
Capture common dependency state before and after
Do not clear dmesg, syslog or SEL
Stop on unexpected device/serial/GPIO/monitoring, boot or recovery behavior
No automatic retry or Load Defaults substitute
Restore and verify baseline when required
agent_execution_scope: Support read-only SUT/SIO identity and dependency collection
Coordinate but do not claim BIOS UI control
Assess only owner-defined affected functions; do not invent a serial test
Track recovery/final state and report without verdict
engineer_actions: Name the common option, values, dependencies, effects and rollback
Resolve unexpected cross-device effects and own PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its NO/manual result is appropriate, but it neither names a safe common field nor defines the proposed serial effect.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Manual operator: capture the named common SIO field and dependencies, change only the approved value, save/reboot/re-enter, prove persistence, observe only specified effects and restore baseline if required.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: SIO Common Setting scope, change/save/re-entry checkpoint and 5/5-minute estimates remain; the missing option becomes an owner input and log clearing is prohibited.

modernized_recommendation.status: MANUAL ONE-FIELD SIO COMMON PERSISTENCE CHECK
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use an evidence tuple of controller identity, common field, baseline/test/restore values, affected-function set, before/save/re-entry/restore captures and boot/dependency health.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Bounds the arbitrary write and distinguishes common controller-wide effects from the next row's per-device configuration coverage.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Persistence proves only the selected common option; physical-port functionality is included only where the owner declares it an effect of that option.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A common SIO control may disable or remap several low-level interfaces and recovery channels simultaneously.

project_override_considerations: A validated remote-console tool can assist evidence capture but does not remove manual ownership of the BIOS write/recovery. The adjacent SIO Configuration row retains independent per-device/port coverage.
expected_evidence: SUT/BIOS/SIO identity, approval and exact common-field matrix
Before, changed, saved/re-entered and restored BIOS captures
Declared dependency set and expected-versus-observed effects, if applicable
Boot/console/SIO health plus preserved event evidence
Recovery/final state and engineer-owned PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently require SIO Common Setting persistence. The exact field and effects are missing readiness inputs, not conflicting requirements; the DeepSeek serial-effect expansion is not treated as Master coverage.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The case is safely defined once the owner identifies one reversible common option, dependencies and recovery path.

review_improvement: Constrains the controller-wide mutation, avoids inventing a serial oracle and separates common-setting persistence from adjacent per-device SIO coverage.
independent_technical_reasoning: A common SIO control can fan out to several device functions, so its risk is defined by dependencies rather than the menu label alone. Persistence of one named value is the direct source requirement; functional observations must be tied to that option's approved dependency model instead of assumed generically.
